title: Back-of-envelope math
short: Estimate traffic and storage in a minute with rounded numbers.
what: Before drawing boxes, estimate how big the system is: requests per second, storage per year. Start from a few stated guesses, round hard, and multiply. The answer tells you if one server is enough or if you need caches and shards.
analogy: Ordering pizza for a party: 30 guests, 3 slices each, 8 slices a pizza, so about 12 pizzas. Nobody counts crumbs.

frames.label: Twitter-like app: estimate
frames.say: Estimate for a Twitter-like app. Start from one guess you can defend out loud: 200 million people use it each day.

frames.label: Twitter-like app: estimate
frames.say: Guess that each one posts 2 times a day on average. Most people only read; a few post a lot.

frames.label: Twitter-like app: estimate
frames.say: Multiply: 400 million new posts a day. Round freely. You want the size of the number, not its last digit.

frames.label: Twitter-like app: estimate
frames.say: A day has 86,400 seconds (call it 100K for mental math). 400M / 86,400 is about 4,600 posts every second.

frames.label: Twitter-like app: estimate
frames.say: Traffic isn't flat over the day. Plan for peaks about 3x the average: roughly 14K writes a second.

frames.label: Twitter-like app: estimate
frames.say: Each post is about 1 KB with its metadata, so 400M posts make 400 GB of new data every day.

frames.label: Twitter-like app: estimate
frames.say: Over 5 years: 400 GB x 365 x 5 is about 730 TB. Far too much for one machine, so plan for sharding.

when: Will one database machine be enough?
The first 5 minutes of any design question
python:
daily_users = 200_000_000
posts_per_user = 2
bytes_per_post = 1_000

posts_per_day = daily_users * posts_per_user
writes_per_sec = posts_per_day / 86_400
peak = writes_per_sec * 3
storage_day = posts_per_day * bytes_per_post
storage_5y = storage_day * 365 * 5

print(f"posts/day:   {posts_per_day / 1e6:,.0f} M")
print(f"writes/sec:  {writes_per_sec:,.0f} (peak {peak:,.0f})")
print(f"storage/day: {storage_day / 1e9:,.0f} GB")
print(f"5 years:     {storage_5y / 1e12:,.0f} TB")
output:
posts/day:   400 M
writes/sec:  4,630 (peak 13,889)
storage/day: 400 GB
5 years:     730 TB
watch: Say your guesses out loud and round hard. The interviewer grades the reasoning, not the digits.
Count reads and writes separately. Reads are often 10-100x more.
Don't forget peaks (x2-3) and copies for safety (x3 replicas).
interview: Design a URL shortener: how many ids in 10 years?
Design YouTube: how much storage a day?
